headline: Argentine sovereign risk surges to 931 bps as Merval and dollar bonds drop
summary: Argentina's country risk index rose nearly 10% to 931 basis points as dollar bonds fell 3% and the MSCI Merval index dropped 2%. Foreign market volatility and domestic exchange rate pressures fueled the downturn.
why: Argentina's sovereign risk index measures the risk premium required by international investors to hold country debt over US Treasuries.

impacts.name: S&P Merval
impacts.why: Currency pressure and international market weakness triggered broad risk reductions in Argentine assets.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Foreign volatility and domestic currency anxiety drove investors away from Argentine stocks and debt securities.
